messages:
pranav: Quick heads up — ran a focused interop probe across Llama2-13B, Mistral-7B, and Qwen-7B comparing rope vs GQA positional norms on H100 (eu-central) and A100 (us-west). Captured q4a/q4m runs and a longseq trace from production.

benchbot: run 2187654321 finished. artifacts: s3://bench/runs/2187654321 (profiles + raw traces).

pranav: High-level surprising bits: Mistral q4m dominates p95 on H100 (≈95ms) but on A100 it regresses to ~180ms due to kernel fallthrough into the interpreter for seq>2048. Qwen shows consistent p99 spikes on H100 when using rope encoding with batch>2. Llama2 has steady throughput but worse latency tail under GQA at 32k context.

maya: Can you paste the condensed numbers? quick list pls. :eyes:

pranav: Sure, trimmed summary (single-token decode p50/p95/p99, seq len 8k trace, bs=1 unless noted):
```
H100-eu:
- Mistral-7B q4m: p50 42ms p95 95ms p99 210ms thrpt 60 seq/s
- Llama2-13B q4a: p50 60ms p95 120ms p99 340ms thrpt 45 seq/s
- Qwen-7B q4a (rope): p50 70ms p95 150ms p99 410ms thrpt 38 seq/s

A100-us:
- Mistral-7B q4m: p50 85ms p95 180ms p99 520ms thrpt 32 seq/s (kernel fallthrough on ctx>2k)
- Llama2-13B q4a: p50 75ms p95 160ms p99 380ms thrpt 40 seq/s
- Qwen-7B q4a (rope): p50 90ms p95 210ms p99 600ms thrpt 28 seq/s
```

pranav: Important note: the A100 Mistral runs dropped into interp for the fused attention path because our kernel selector mis-classified the model as having unsupported ROPE stride (due to nonstandard token embeddings).

liam: Oof. How deterministic is that classifier? Sounds like a config mismatch more than HW-limited.

pranav: It's borderline — selector checks posenc metadata and a fast checksum of attention config. Qwen's rope implementation uses rolling-window meta which trips the check. We saw the same checksum mismatch in a small subset of Llama variants but fallthrough logic was cheaper there. For Mistral, the fused kernel would have been 2-3x faster so fallthrough hurts the tail.

jen: Any visual of the tail? p99 spike distribution?

pranav: Uploaded p95/p99 time series to the run artifacts. Short paste here for H100 Mistral vs A100 Mistral p99 over time (excerpt):
```
timestamp, h100_p99_ms, a100_p99_ms
00:00, 210, 520
00:30, 205, 540
01:00, 215, 600 (spike correlated with ctxsplit fallback)
```

maya: ctxsplit fallback — is that the request that tried to force >16k context?

pranav: Yes. We had a synthetic longseq trace with bursts up to 32k. On A100 the kernel selector opted to ctxsplit (two-phase) + interp path which amplified overhead: extra memcpy + repeated kv setup.

liam: So action items? Sounds like two fronts: selector heuristics + quant kernel compatibility checks.

pranav: Agreed. Proposed short list:
- Add stronger posenc compatibility unit test into model onboarding to catch rolling-window rope variants.
- Add a telemetry tag when fallthrough happens so we can correlate model/version/seq distribution.
- Run a targeted microbench for Mistral on A100 with patched selector (force fused) to measure real delta.
- Re-run Qwen rope runs with bs=2 and batch-scheduling tweak (we saw tail sensitivity to batch coalescing).

jen: For the microbench, I can spin a couple of dedicated hosts in us-west with pinned drivers. Want me to do that and run the 'force-fused' job?

pranav: Please. Use run config:
```
--model mistral-7b --quant q4m --force-fused-kernel true --seq-len 8192 --bs 1 --trace 1
```
And capture nvprof + kernel selection logs.

benchbot: queued job 2187654330 on a100-us-dedicated-1 (ETA 12m).

maya: small ask — include a run with 'kv-eviction=early' to see if prefix caching changes the tail. Qwen rope spikes might be KV related.

pranav: Good call. I'll add that to the baseline set.

liam: Also add a deterministic checksum override param so model onboarding can force-accept nonstandard rope by hash during canary tests. But gate it behind a safety flag.

jen: On it. I'll collect driver/kernel versions and confirm there's no ABI mismatch. If fused kernel is ABI-sensitive it could explain some of the A100 regressions although selector mismatch seems primary.

pranav: Cool. Once we have the forced-fused microbench numbers we can decide whether to relax selector or add model-specific kernel pathways. If fused gives expected 2-3x p95 improvement on A100, we push a selector patch + add a regression eval in onboarding.

maya: Thanks — this is a great repro. Can someone create a short PR checklist for onboarding to catch this class of issue? I'll own the checklist.

pranav: I'll drop the run links and raw traces in the ticket. tagging @maya @jen @liam for followup. :thumbsup:

benchbot: job 2187654330 started on a100-us-dedicated-1. logs: s3://bench/runs/2187654330/logs

jen: Nice. I'll monitor and we can sync tomorrow in the daily ML standup if needed.
